data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements_

**Class:** Trace element (antioxidant; component of glutathione peroxidase)

## Mechanism of action
- Part of selenoproteins (glutathione peroxidase, thioredoxin reductase) that protect against oxidative/UV damage

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Selenium deficiency (long-term parenteral nutrition, Keshan disease): leuconychia, hair and skin hypopigmentation, cardiomyopathy
- Adjunct antioxidant in vitiligo, psoriasis, polymorphous light eruption (limited evidence)
- Thyroid eye disease (mild — selenium 100 µg twice daily)

## Dose & formulations
- 50–200 µg/day (do not exceed 400 µg/day)

## Adverse effects
- Selenosis (excess): garlic breath, brittle nails and hair loss, skin rash, neuropathy; possible higher diabetes and skin cancer risk with long-term supplements

## Contraindications
- Excess intake

## Pregnancy & lactation
Dietary amounts safe.

## Viva points
- Selenosis — garlic breath, nail and hair loss
- Do not confuse with selenium sulfide shampoo

_Sources: Khopkar (Trace elements — selenium). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
